name: שני מישורים במרחב – מצב הדדי, זווית ומרחק (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Two planes in \(R^3\) assume one of three possible mutual configurations. All three are demonstrated by this little figure as follows:

(1) The planes \(X\) and \(Y\) are parallel, (2) The planes \(X\) and \(Z\) intersect in a line, (3) The plane \(X\) coincides with itself.

Consider the affine plane \(P_1\) passing through the three points \(u_1={{CT:0}}, u_2={{CT:1}}, u_3={{CT:2}}\) and a second plane defined by the equation \(P_2: \left\{v \in R^3 \ | \ v \cdot {{CT:3}} = {{CT:4}} \right\} \). Let us investigate some geometric questions. This time we provide less information than before - leaving the tasks to you. Try to use methods similar to these that we used in the previous questions.

a

What is the cosine of the angle between the two planes (note that this is the same as the angles between the normal vectors to the two planes).

\(cos(\angle(P_1, P_2)) = \) [[input:ans2]]
[[validation:ans2]]
b

What is the mutual configuration (enter a number 1=parallel, 2=intersecting, 3=coincident):

[[input:ans3]]
[[validation:ans3]]
c

What is the distance between \(P_1\) and \(P_2\)

[[input:ans4]]
[[validation:ans4]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Find a normal vector of each plane. The angle between the normals gives the cosine; parallel normals mean parallel or coincident planes, and only then is the distance positive.
Step 1 — Normal vectors
The vectors \(u_2-u_1\) and \(u_3-u_1\) lie in \(P_1\) and are not parallel, so their cross product is a normal vector of \(P_1\):

\[ N_1=(u_2-u_1)\times(u_3-u_1)={{CT:5}}\times{{CT:6}}={{CT:7}} \]

The plane \(P_2\) is given by \(v\cdot n_2=c_2\) with \(n_2={{CT:3}}\) and \(c_2={{CT:4}}\). Its coefficient vector \(n_2\) is a normal vector: if \(v,v'\in P_2\) then \(n_2\cdot(v-v')=c_2-c_2=0\).
Step 2 — The cosine of the angle (part a)
The angle between the planes is the angle between their normals:

\[ \cos(\angle(P_1,P_2))=\frac{N_1\cdot n_2}{\|N_1\|\,\|n_2\|}=\frac{{{CT:8}}}{[[if test="{{CT:17}}"]]{{CT:9}}[[else]]\sqrt{{{CT:10}}}[[/if]]\cdot[[if test="{{CT:18}}"]]{{CT:11}}[[else]]\sqrt{{{CT:12}}}[[/if]]}={{CT:13}} \]

(Taking \(-N_1\) instead of \(N_1\) only changes the sign, so the opposite value describes the same pair of planes.)
Step 3 — The mutual configuration (part b)
[[if test="{{CT:19}}"]]The cosine is not \(\pm 1\), so the normals are not parallel. Hence the planes are not parallel, and two non-parallel planes intersect in a line: the configuration is

\[ 2\ \text{(intersecting)} \]

[[else]]The cosine is \(\pm 1\), so the normals are parallel: the planes are parallel or coincide. To decide, check whether the point \(u_1\) of \(P_1\) satisfies the equation of \(P_2\):

\[ u_1\cdot n_2={{CT:14}},\qquad c_2={{CT:4}} \]

[[if test="{{CT:20}}"]]The values are equal, so \(u_1\in P_2\) and the planes coincide: the configuration is

\[ 3\ \text{(coincident)} \]

[[else]]The values differ, so \(u_1\notin P_2\) and the planes are parallel: the configuration is

\[ 1\ \text{(parallel)} \]

[[/if]][[/if]]
Step 4 — The distance (part c)
[[if test="{{CT:21}}"]]The planes are parallel, so every point of \(P_1\) is at the same distance from \(P_2\). For the point \(u_1\), the distance is the absolute value of \(u_1\cdot n_2-c_2\) divided by \(\|n_2\|\) (the length of the projection on \(n_2\) of the vector from a point of \(P_2\) to \(u_1\)):

\[ d=\frac{|{{CT:15}}|}{[[if test="{{CT:18}}"]]{{CT:11}}[[else]]\sqrt{{{CT:12}}}[[/if]]}={{CT:16}} \]

[[else]]The planes have common points, so the distance between them is

\[ d={{CT:16}} \]

[[/if]]

on_true.feedback: Part a — correct. You found the correct cosine of the angle between the two planes.
Part a — correct. You found the correct cosine of the angle between the two planes.

on_false.feedback: Part a — incorrect. No this is not the correct cosine of the angle between the two planes.

on_true.feedback: Part b — correct. Yes, you found the correct mutual configuration of \(P_1\) and \(P_2\).

on_false.feedback: Part b — incorrect. No, you did not find the correct mutual configuration of \(P_1\) and \(P_2\). Please try again.

on_true.feedback: Part c — correct. Yes, you calculated the distance correctly.

on_false.feedback: Part c — incorrect. No you got the wrong distance, please try again.
